summary: Serves as a guide to implementing a Transport Services system, which provides the protocol-independent Transport Services API based on an asynchronous, event-driven pattern. It is informational.

eli5.summary: This is a how-to for builders of the system that picks the right delivery method for an app.

questions: how to select protocols for connection
subtitle: Guide to implementing a system that selects and manages transport protocols for applications.

tldr.problem: Applications need to use diverse transport protocols flexibly, but building systems that select protocols and paths intelligently is complex and inconsistent across platforms.
tldr.mechanism: A Transport Services implementation provides the underlying system that takes application requirements and automatically selects and manages the best transport protocol stack and network path for communication.
tldr.outcome: Applications can focus on their functionality while the Transport Services system handles protocol selection, connection establishment, and multipath management. This guide helps implementers build these systems correctly.

today: RFC 9623 is an Informational RFC published in January 2025. It provides the implementation guide for Transport Services systems, complementing RFC 9621 (architecture) and RFC 9622 (API). Multiple implementations of Transport Services are in development.

sections.title: Transport Services Implementation Overview
sections.content:
A Transport Services System implements the Transport Services API, which allows applications to request transport communication using abstract properties rather than choosing specific protocols directly. The implementation's job is to translate these abstract requirements into decisions about which protocols to use, which network paths to attempt, and how to establish and manage connections.

The system must handle three layers of properties: application preferences (stated via the API), dynamic system policy (based on current network state and OS policy), and default implementation policy. These are combined to determine which protocols and paths are eligible for a connection.

This implementation guide provides practical recommendations for how to structure a Transport Services System, including how to gather candidate protocols and paths, how to race multiple connection attempts, and how to manage established connections.
sections.eli5: A Transport Services implementation is the system that makes smart choices about how to send data. It checks what the app needs, what the network can do, and what policies are in place, then picks the best way to send the data.

sections.title: Connection Objects and Establishment
sections.content:
Transport Services exposes three main objects to applications: the Preconnection (a bundle of properties describing what the connection should do), the Connection (the actual communication channel), and the Listener (for accepting incoming connections).

Connection establishment is divided into two phases: Candidate Gathering and Candidate Racing. During gathering, the implementation identifies which network paths, protocols, and endpoints are available and eligible based on application requirements and system policy. During racing, the implementation attempts multiple candidates and uses the first one that succeeds.

To manage complex scenarios with multiple paths (Wi-Fi and Cellular), multiple resolved addresses (IPv4 and IPv6), and multiple protocol options (TCP vs QUIC), the implementation can conceptually structure candidates as a tree where each leaf node represents a complete, specific connection attempt.
sections.eli5: Before sending data, the system prepares a plan with three parts: list everything available (Wi-Fi or cellular, different addresses), try multiple approaches (TCP or QUIC), and use whichever one works first.

sections.title: Candidate Gathering and Racing Strategies
sections.content:
Candidate Gathering involves discovering which paths, protocols, and endpoints are available. Local endpoint gathering discovers all usable local network interfaces and addresses. Remote endpoint gathering resolves hostnames to IP addresses and may involve services like ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) for peer-to-peer scenarios. Branches in the candidate tree include derived endpoints (DNS results), network paths (different interfaces), and protocol options (different protocol stacks).

During Candidate Racing, implementations attempt multiple candidates and select the first to succeed. The racing strategy can be simultaneous (start all at once, wasteful), staggered (start after delays, balanced), or failover (only start if previous fails, conservative). Staggered racing is recommended for most use cases. The timing between attempts should account for expected handshake latency and path preparation time.

Implementations should maintain performance caches that track which protocols and paths work well on specific networks, allowing future connections to prioritize historically successful options.
sections.eli5: The system makes a list of ways to connect (gather), then tries them one by one with small delays between tries (race). If Wi-Fi is faster to set up, try it first; if it fails, try Cellular. Remember which worked best for next time.

sections.title: Sending, Receiving, and Message Framing
sections.content:
Once a connection is established, applications send and receive messages. The top-level protocol in the Protocol Stack determines what a Message represents: for datagram protocols like UDP, each message is a single packet; for byte-stream protocols like TCP, a complete stream is one message; for framing protocols, a message is a frame.

Message Properties allow applications to attach metadata to individual messages, such as lifetime limits, reliability requirements, ordering preferences, and whether they are safely replayable. These properties influence how the Transport Services System and underlying protocols handle each message.

Message Framers are optional protocol layers that applications or the implementation can add to define custom message formatting. A Framer can handle encoding/decoding messages, implementing protocol handshakes (like STARTTLS), or performing custom message parsing. Framers participate in sender-side encoding and receiver-side parsing, and can transition to passthrough mode once setup is complete.
sections.eli5: The system can send messages with special instructions attached: how important they are, whether they need to arrive in order, or how long they can wait. Custom message formatters can be added to handle special message types or protocols.

sections.title: Connection Management and Path Changes
sections.content:
After a connection is established, the Transport Services System must manage various aspects of its lifetime. The implementation can modify connection properties to adjust protocol behavior, handle soft errors from the underlying protocols, and manage error events delivered to applications.

When the network changes (path becomes unavailable, new interface appears), the implementation must respond appropriately. For protocols that do not support multipath or migration, temporary path losses should not cause immediate disconnection, as the path may recover before timeouts occur. For protocols supporting multipath or migration, new paths should be made available so the transport can adapt.

Pooled Connections allow the implementation to distribute messages of a single logical connection across multiple underlying transport connections or streams, without requiring in-order delivery. This is useful for request-response protocols like HTTP where this distribution is transparent to the application.

The implementation should cache protocol state (DNS results, TLS tickets, TCP Fast Open cookies) and performance metrics (RTT, bandwidth, success rates) to guide future connection establishment attempts.
sections.eli5: After connecting, the system watches for network changes, remembers what worked well, and stores certificates or cookies for faster reconnection next time. If the network disappears temporarily, it waits instead of giving up immediately.
